cards.summary: 【The Verge】I would prefer that these people's sex lives were none of my business but I guess we have to talk about Jensen Huang and the National Security Incident. Who could have guessed that the guy who was out…
fulltext: NVIDIOT.

I would prefer that these people’s sex lives were none of my business but I guess we have to talk about Jensen Huang and the National Security Incident. Who could have guessed that the guy who was out here signing titties might not have great judgment about how to behave around women?

Alice Huang — no relation to Jensen — is a former TV reporter. That was before she became “an executive” at Megaspeed, which bought $4.8 billion of hard-to-get Nvidia chips, starting around the time she was being photographed with Jensen in a Taipei bar in 2024. “To many in the industry, the well-funded push by Megaspeed into A.I. appeared to come out of nowhere,” The New York Times wrote, tactfully. Our girl Alice is also an alleged honeypot who was recruited by the Chinese Ministry of State Security. (China is denying all this, btw.)
You know shit is going good when your corporate spokesperson has to tell the Times that of course your company does not disclose classified information to your customers

What is Megaspeed? Well. The company has ties to the Chinese military and builds data centers in “Southeast Asia” (it has offices in Singapore and Indonesia) to sell compute to Alibaba. The chips it is using to do that are banned from being imported to China. Incidentally, Nvidia has been lobbying very intensely to get rid of import controls on its chips so it can sell them in China.

This is all public knowledge in part because Secretary of State Marco Rubio reportedly “oversaw” a memo detailing Alice’s recruitment and relationship with Jensen, and then someone leaked it. (Powerful memo game, Marco, getting credit for one you didn’t even write!) Rubio passed his little note around in May, ahead of a trip to China taken by President Donald Trump. Jensen initially didn’t make the list of invitees on the trip — at least, not until Trump saw media coverage of the perceived snub. Trump and Jensen? They’re close. Which makes it even more interesting that Trump was personally briefed on the findings and did nothing, according to the Times.

You know shit is going good when your corporate spokesperson has to tell the Times that of course your company does not disclose classified information to your customers. John Rizzo, the spokesman, also told the Times that Nvidia’s customers don’t ask Nvidia to lobby for changes to the chip restriction. Bit of a hat on a hat, John. First of all, they don’t have to — Nvidia’s financial incentives do it for them. Second, imagine this is a regular company. The business model of Megaspeed is that the chips are restricted, and that Megaspeed gets ahold of them. Megaspeed has no incentive to upend this situation! Unless, you know, it’s acting against its financial interest because it’s a front for Chinese spies… in which case, that statement is going to be embarrassing.

Speaking of embarrassing, Rizzo told the Times “that Mr. Huang’s interactions with Ms. Huang were ‘not unusual’ and consistent with the kinds of meetings he has with any of Nvidia’s many customers.” Oh, okay. Who else was Jensen fucking?
Nvidia has an extraordinary structure

Because two days after that statement, Jensen sent the most incredible email addressed “To my colleagues at Nvidia” in which he admitted he had been “unfaithful.” Then, he wrote, “To my wife and family: I love you. I know an apology cannot undo what I have done. I hope our family will heal and that, over time, I can earn back your trust.” Are… your wife and family on the Nvidia employee email list?
Well, yes! His son is a director of product management; his daughter is a senior marketing director. He even gave a job to his son-in-law!

Also, Nvidia has an extraordinary structure. Jensen has 60 direct reports. Leave aside that there is no possible way to manage that many people well. I would like to direct your attention to something else entirely: If he is in trouble, there is no part of the company that is untouched. The usual problems attain, of course — he was in a position to have gotten any information she might have requested! He could have left company laptops available for infiltration! But because of the structure, he also could have issued commands to his many direct reports that benefited the CCP. Neat! I sure hope someone who knows a lot about cybersecurity is going through Nvidia with a fine-toothed comb.

Is he in trouble? Well, Nvidia is opening an investigation into Jensen, who is also its largest individual shareholder. (At least there’s no dual-class stock!) Nvidia shares are, as of this writing, down almost five percent, which seems like an underreaction.
I don’t know where Jensen’s actual wife, Lori, is in all this

Perhaps more consequentially, the Democratic Party just swept back into power and Sen. Elizabeth Warren (D-MA) seems mad. Also, the voters hate the data centers that house Nvidia chips, and I notice a lot of ambitious politicians thinking about the next presidential elections. For instance, there’s Rubio’s name attached to the memo. I also notice Trump’s popularity is at an all-time nadir. Besides any Democrats positioning themselves for a run, a Republican looking to create some daylight between himself and Trump could easily do so by going to town on Jensen, who is Trump’s buddy. I do not think Rubio is the only ambition monster to worry about.

I don’t know where Jensen’s actual wife, Lori, is in all this. They got married in 1985. She gave up her job as a microchip designer to raise their kids. I would be very surprised if there is a prenup. I would be somewhat surprised if there was a postnup. Jensen doesn’t own as much of Nvidia as Jeff Bezos did of Amazon when he cheated on and divorced his wife, but it’s something to keep an eye on, if Lori decides she’s out.

We’ve talked once or twice about Nvidia’s central role in the AI ecosystem — and specifically, that it is heavily involved in financing AI neoclouds. It has investments in SpaceX, CoreWeave (where it was, as of the time of the IPO, the company’s second-biggest customer), and OpenAI, among others. Jensen has been promoting “compute as an asset class.”
Nvidia is, effectively, the central bank of AI

One of the reasons I have been uncertain about when and how the AI bubble will pop is that it seems to me that Nvidia can bail out any or all of these companies anytime it needs to, just like it did for CoreWeave when its IPO was threatened. Neoclouds exist because Nvidia wanted to create competition for its chips, so its biggest customers — Microsoft, Amazon, Google, Oracle — couldn’t exert too much pricing pressure. Certainly I am not the only person who has noticed that Nvidia is, effectively, the central bank of AI. If Nvidia is in a particularly bad way, it kind of seems like, at minimum, the neoclouds get fucked too. Oddly, CoreWeave is up about 6 percent as of this writing; the stock market moves in mysterious ways.

Maybe that is why our nation’s foremost thought leaders on X are posting things like “Whomst among us hasn’t accidentally fucked a Chinese spy? That’s how it is on this bitch of an earth.” I’m kidding, here’s investor/loudmouth Bill Ackman: “We should all support him and his family. Onward.” Shaun Maguire, partner at VC firm Sequoia: “I believe Jensen is irreplaceable for America’s AI leadership.” (Elon Musk took a quick break from complaining about Dave Chappelle’s comedy to type “I agree” to Maguire’s note.)

So Jensen can’t go down, as there’s no one who can replace him, and Nvidia can’t go down, as nothing can replace it. The AI industry better hope there isn’t some further revelation coming that would make one of these things unavoidable, such as the investigation finding proof that Alice directly accessed Nvidia’s systems while Jensen was showering or something. Might also be bad if, say, a US Commerce Department inquiry into Megaspeed was halted after Nvidia intervened. Didn’t we just hear somewhere that Jensen had been influencing the Trump administration’s policy on export controls?

Anyway, as of this note, Jensen isn’t planning to step down as CEO. Might as well settle in for the most fun we’ll have until we find out that Musk did IVF with a family member of Chinese President Xi Jinping.

cards.summary_cn: 【The Verge】我宁愿这些人的性生活不关我的事，但我想我们必须谈谈黄仁勋和国安事件。谁能想到，那个出去的人……
fulltext_cn: NVIDIO。
我宁愿这些人的性生活不关我的事，但我想我们必须谈谈黄仁勋和国安事件。谁能想到，这个在外面签乳头的家伙可能对如何在女性面前表现没有很好的判断力？

艾丽丝·黄（Alice Huang）——与詹森没有关系——是一名前电视记者。那是在她成为 Megaspeed 的“高管”之前，Megaspeed 购买了价值 48 亿美元的难以获得的 Nvidia 芯片，大约是在 2024 年她与 Jensen 在台北一家酒吧被拍到的时候开始的。“对业内许多人来说，Megaspeed 资金充足的进军人工智能似乎是凭空而来，”《纽约时报》巧妙地写道。我们的女孩Alice也是被中国国家安全部招募的所谓蜜罐。 （顺便说一句，中国否认这一切。）
当你的公司发言人必须告诉《纽约时报》，你的公司当然不会向你的客户透露机密信息时，你就知道事情进展顺利了
什么是兆速？出色地。该公司与中国军方有联系，并在“东南亚”建立数据中心（在新加坡和印度尼西亚设有办事处），向阿里巴巴出售计算机。它用来做这些事情的芯片被禁止进口到中国。顺便说一句，英伟达一直在大力游说，要求取消其芯片的进口管制，以便能够在中国销售它们。

这些都是公众所知，部分原因是国务卿马可·鲁比奥据报道“监督”了一份详细说明爱丽丝的招募以及与詹森关系的备忘录，然后有人泄露了它。 （马可，强大的备忘录游戏，你甚至没有写的一篇文章就得到了赞扬！）卢比奥在五月唐纳德·特朗普总统访问中国之前传递了他的小便条。詹森最初并没有出现在这次旅行的受邀者名单中——至少直到特朗普看到媒体对他的冷落报道之后才出现。特朗普和詹森？他们很接近。据《泰晤士报》报道，更有趣的是，特朗普亲自听取了调查结果的简报，但没有采取任何行动。

当你的公司发言人必须告诉《纽约时报》，你的公司当然不会向你的客户透露机密信息时，你就知道事情进展顺利了。发言人约翰·里佐 (John Rizzo) 还告诉《泰晤士报》，英伟达的客户不会要求英伟达游说改变芯片限制。约翰，有点帽子上的帽子。首先，他们不必这么做——英伟达的经济激励措施已经为他们做到了这一点。其次，想象这是一家普通公司。 Megaspeed的商业模式是芯片受到限制，Megaspeed获得芯片。 Megaspeed 没有动力去扭转这种局面！除非，你知道，它的行为违背了其经济利益，因为它是中国间谍的幌子……在这种情况下，该声明将会令人尴尬。
谈到尴尬，里佐告诉《泰晤士报》，“黄先生与黄女士的互动‘并不罕见’，并且与他与 Nvidia 众多客户的会议类型一致。”哦好的。 Jensen他妈的还有谁？
Nvidia 拥有非凡的架构
因为在发表声明两天后，詹森发送了一封最令人难以置信的电子邮件，地址是“致我在英伟达的同事”，他在邮件中承认自己“不忠”。然后，他写道：“致我的妻子和家人：我爱你们。我知道道歉无法挽回我所做的一切。我希望我们的家人能够痊愈，随着时间的推移，我可以赢回你们的信任。”您的妻子和家人在 Nvidia 员工电子邮件列表中吗？
嗯，是的！他的儿子是产品管理总监；他的女儿是一名高级营销总监。还把工作让给了自己的女婿！

此外，Nvidia 还拥有非凡的结构。 Jensen 有 60 名直接下属。且不说，没有办法管理好这么多人。我想把你的注意力转移到完全不同的事情上：如果他遇到麻烦，公司的任何部分都会受到影响。当然，常见的问题出现了——他能够得到她可能要求的任何信息！他本可以留下公司的笔记本电脑以供渗透！但由于这种结构，他也可以向他的许多直接下属发出对中共有利的命令。整洁的！我当然希望对网络安全了解很多的人能够仔细研究 Nvidia。
他有麻烦吗？ Nvidia 正在对 Jensen 展开调查，他也是该公司最大的个人股东。 （至少没有双重股权股票！）截至撰写本文时，Nvidia 股价已下跌近 5%，这似乎反应不足。
我不知道 Jensen 真正的妻子 Lori 在这一切中在哪里

也许更重要的是，民主党刚刚重新掌权，参议员伊丽莎白·沃伦 (D-MA) 似乎很生气。此外，选民讨厌装有英伟达芯片的数据中心，我注意到很多雄心勃勃的政客正在考虑下一次总统选举。 For instance, there’s Rubio’s name attached to the memo.我还注意到特朗普的支持率正处于历史最低点。 Besides any Democrats positioning themselves for a run, a Republican looking to create some daylight between himself and Trump could easily do so by going to town on Jensen, who is Trump’s buddy.我不认为卢比奥是唯一值得担心的野心怪物。
我不知道 Jensen 真正的妻子 Lori 在这一切中处于什么位置。他们于 1985 年结婚。她放弃了微芯片设计师的工作来抚养孩子。如果有婚前协议，我会感到非常惊讶。如果有婚后协议，我会有点惊讶。詹森所拥有的英伟达股份并不像杰夫·贝佐斯在背叛妻子并与妻子离婚时所拥有的亚马逊那么多，但如果洛里决定退出，这就是值得关注的事情。
我们已经谈论过英伟达在人工智能生态系统中的核心作用，特别是它积极参与人工智能新云的融资。它投资了 SpaceX、CoreWeave（截至 IPO 时，它是该公司的第二大客户）和 OpenAI 等。 Jensen 一直在提倡“计算作为一种资产类别”。
Nvidia 实际上是人工智能的中央银行

我一直不确定人工智能泡沫何时以及如何破灭的原因之一是，在我看来，Nvidia 可以在需要时随时救助任何或所有这些公司，就像 CoreWeave 在 IPO 受到威胁时所做的那样。 Neoclouds 的存在是因为英伟达希望为其芯片创造竞争，因此其最大的客户——微软、亚马逊、谷歌、甲骨文——无法施加太大的定价压力。当然，我并不是唯一一个注意到 Nvidia 实际上是人工智能中央银行的人。如果 Nvidia 的情况特别糟糕，那么至少 Neocloud 似乎也会完蛋。奇怪的是，截至撰写本文时，CoreWeave 上涨了约 6%；股市以神秘的方式波动。

也许这就是为什么我们国家最重要的思想领袖在 X 上发布诸如“我们当中谁没有不小心操过中国间谍？地球上就是这样。”之类的内容。我开玩笑的，投资人兼大嘴比尔·阿克曼（Bill Ackman）说道：“我们都应该支持他和他的家人。继续前进。”风险投资公司红杉资本合伙人肖恩·马奎尔（Shaun Maguire）：“我相信詹森对于美国人工智能的领导地位是不可替代的。” （埃隆·马斯克在抱怨戴夫·查佩尔的喜剧后短暂休息了一下，在马奎尔的便条上输入了“我同意”。）
所以 Jensen 不能倒下，因为没有人可以取代他，Nvidia 也不能倒下，因为没有人可以取代它。人工智能行业最好希望不会出现任何进一步的披露，使这些事情变得不可避免，例如调查发现证据表明爱丽丝在詹森洗澡时直接访问了英伟达的系统或其他什么。如果美国商务部对 Megaspeed 的调查在英伟达介入后停止，情况也可能很糟糕。我们不是刚刚在某处听说詹森一直在影响特朗普政府的出口管制政策吗？
无论如何，截至本文为止，詹森并不打算辞去首席执行官职务。在我们发现马斯克与中国国家主席习近平的家人进行试管受精之前，我们不妨先享受一下最有趣的事情。

Online publishing platform Medium on Monday launched a new app, called TK, which aims to bring AI technology deeper into the writing process. The idea behind TK is to make it easier to turn ideas into written words by incorporating an AI assistant into the editor itself, allowing users to ask for help by typing “@TK” followed by their request or prompt.

In publishing and journalism, the term “TK” serves as a placeholder used to mark where missing information can be added later. The “TK” stands for “to come,” but uses a “K” instead of “C” as there are few English words where the “tk” letter combination exists, making it stand out more easily in written text where it could be caught by proofreaders.
In Medium’s app, TK takes on a new role as it tries to help users fill in the blanks.

The company suggests the AI assistant could help answer questions that you might normally have to switch to another tab to quickly look up, like how many days are in a particular month. The app could also pull in bits of writing you had previously saved to the app when you were still fleshing out your ideas.
In addition, Medium says TK will ship with particular skills for editorial feedback, headline feedback, and others that could match your draft to the style guide for Medium publications.

Medium’s move to embrace AI in the early stages of writing could prove controversial at a time when the publishing and literary worlds have been reckoning with the role that artificial intelligence has played in the creation of new long-form prose. Multiple authors have lost book deals over suspicions that they used AI technology to help them write, while other literary awards have come under scrutiny after winners were suspected of writing with AI assistance.

While writers have long used automated tools for proofreading and light grammatical edits, there is growing concern across the publishing industry that an AI assistant’s editorial “suggestions” can become the writing itself, instead of being reflective of the thoughts in the writer’s own mind.

But because AI models were trained on human writing, there are also questions around the reliability of AI detection tools in terms of their ability to properly determine when something was written with AI, rather than with its assistance, versus not at all.

TK leans into this debate, taking the side that these nuances will ultimately no longer matter in the end. Instead, the company celebrates what AI can bring to the world of writing, saying that “artificial intelligence makes writing more important, not less,” and proclaiming that “AI is a technology that has the power to amplify human intelligence and it uses the written word as a foundation.”

Still, Medium concedes that AI does raise the possibility of low-quality content and blurring the line between what’s human-written versus AI-written. To address these concerns, TK allows authors to publish notes that transparently explain how AI was used in their writing.

“This is a start of what we believe is required to publish in the AI era, which is to make the provenance of writing clear, transparent, and inspectable, right down to the prompting and source material,” Medium explained in a blog post about the launch.

In addition to writing assistance, TK will help users remember and organize what they had previously written and suggest writing prompts. The app can also optionally connect to your own AI agent through TK’s MCP server or Claude skill, so the app can better understand your projects, your positions, and other ideas that could be stored in your agent’s memory.
Meanwhile, the new app incorporates human feedback in a social layer, the company says, allowing writers to share their early drafts with others and get feedback.

At launch, TK is available on the web, but a desktop app is on the roadmap, Medium says. The app can import and export Markdown, but it’s not a Markdown app itself. The writing in TK is also not encrypted, as the app is designed for collaboration, but users will be able to set access control permissions on their work.
Medium, which is profitable, says TK will be a free tool for those with a Medium account.

在线出版平台Medium周一推出了一款名为TK的新应用程序，旨在将人工智能技术更深入地引入写作过程。传统知识背后的想法是通过将人工智能助手整合到编辑器中，使用户可以通过键入“@ TK” ，然后输入他们的请求或提示来寻求帮助，从而更容易地将想法转化为书面文字。
在出版和新闻业中， “传统知识”一词用作占位符，用于标记可以在以后添加缺失信息的位置。“TK”代表“to come” ，但使用“K”而不是“C” ，因为存在“tk”字母组合的英语单词很少，这使得它更容易在书面文本中脱颖而出，校对者可以抓住它。
在Medium的应用程序中， TK扮演了一个新的角色，因为它试图帮助用户填补空白。
该公司建议，人工智能助手可以帮助回答您通常需要切换到另一个选项卡才能快速查找的问题，例如特定月份有多少天。应用程序还可以将您之前在充实创意时保存到应用程序的文字提取出来。
此外， Medium表示， TK将在编辑反馈、标题反馈和其他可能与Medium出版物风格指南相匹配的技能方面提供特定的技能。
Medium在写作的早期阶段拥抱人工智能的举动可能会引起争议，因为出版和文学界一直在考虑人工智能在创造新的长篇散文中所扮演的角色。多位作者因怀疑他们使用人工智能技术帮助他们写作而失去了书籍交易，而其他文学奖项在获奖者被怀疑在人工智能协助下写作后受到审查。
虽然作家长期以来一直使用自动化工具进行校对和轻度语法编辑，但整个出版行业越来越担心人工智能助理的编辑“建议”可能成为写作本身，而不是反映作家自己头脑中的想法。
但由于人工智能模型是经过人工写作训练的，因此也存在人工智能检测工具的可靠性问题，因为它们能够正确确定何时使用人工智能而不是人工智能辅助写作，而不是完全没有。
传统知识倾向于这场辩论，认为这些细微差别最终将不再重要。相反，该公司庆祝人工智能可以为写作世界带来什么，称“人工智能使写作更重要，而不是更不重要” ，并宣称“人工智能是一种有能力放大人类智能的技术，它使用书面文字作为基础。”
尽管如此， Medium承认，人工智能确实提高了低质量内容的可能性，并模糊了人工写作和人工智能写作之间的界限。为了解决这些问题， TK允许作者发布透明地解释如何在写作中使用AI的笔记。
Medium在关于发布的博客文章中解释说： “这是我们认为在人工智能时代发布所需的开始，这是为了使写作的来源清晰、透明和可检验，直至提示和源材料。”
除了写作帮助外， TK还将帮助用户记住和组织他们之前写过的内容，并提出写作提示。该应用程序还可以选择通过TK的MCP服务器或Claude技能连接到您自己的AI代理，因此该应用程序可以更好地了解您的项目、您的职位以及可能存储在代理记忆中的其他想法。
与此同时，该公司表示，新应用程序将人工反馈纳入社交层，允许作家与他人分享他们的早期草稿并获得反馈。
Medium说，在发布时， TK可以在网络上获得，但桌面应用程序已经在路线图上。应用程序可以导入和导出Markdown ，但它本身不是Markdown应用程序。传统知识的书写也未加密，因为该应用程序专为协作而设计，但用户将能够为其工作设置访问控制权限。
盈利的Medium表示，对于拥有Medium账户的人来说， TK将是一个免费的工具。

fulltext: Trump claims the DOJ told a top AI executive, ‘get ready to go to jail.’

Asked about AI executives’ warnings about their models’ safety on 60 Minutes, Trump said, “I think that the risk is not nearly as real as it– as they talk, and I think the risk can be managed, and it’s managed.” He claimed the DOJ is managing that risk, saying, “We had a situation where somebody was reported to us to be doing something bad with AI. We called them very strongly and said, ‘Get ready to go to jail. Please give your wife a kiss good night.’”

Trump refused to name the person or company he was referring to, but said it was the leader of an AI company, “One of the big ones.” He claimed that after the threat of arrest, “this person totally changed everything.” Despite previously claiming that “artificial intelligence” is a term used by people he considers the enemy, Trump said AI rather than SI or super intelligence multiple times during the interview. Eventually he said China’s Xi is “…all in to SI, as I call it, because it really is super intelligence. It’s a much better name, I think, because it’s not artificial.”

60 Minutes’s Ross Douthat went on to ask if Trump would work with Democrats on AI safety, and Trump said he “absolutely would,” adding, “I don’t mind guardrails, but I don’t want to put us in a deep second position. We’re leading number one. And China has no guardrails, by the way. [...] They have the guardrails that whatever President Xi says goes. With me, it’s pretty strong, but it’s not quite that strong.”

Olivia Dean is Apple Music’s Artist of the Year for 2026

Olivia Dean was announced today as Apple Music’s Artist of the Year, recognizing her undeniable leap to stardom in what’s been the defining feel-good music story of 2026. She is the first UK artist to receive this honor.

Olivia’s late 2025 album, The Art of Loving, truly broke through this year. Her hit “Man I Need” has charted on Apple Music’s Daily Top 100 every day since first appearing on August 29, 2025. In addition to selling out her global tour, she won a GRAMMY for Best New Artist and four BRIT Awards, including Artist of the Year. In fall 2025, Olivia opened for Sabrina Carpenter at Madison Square Garden, in New York City. Less than a year later, she returned for her own four-night residency and followed up with a six-night sold-out run at The O2 Arena, in London.

Olivia has found and grown her audience with warm, vulnerable songs about love and friendship. Apple Music editors have highlighted the grace with which her music taps into the rich songwriting tradition of 1960s soul and pop, and is inspired by the sensuality of Sade, the brazenness of Prince, and the honesty of Lauryn Hill — all while fostering a community built on love. Olivia’s messages of affirmation and connection resonate deeply with her fans. Listeners have responded to her worldview that expressing love, in all its forms, is an active practice that takes conscious effort, an idea inspired by the 1999 book All About Love: New Visions, by bell hooks.

“I love making music,” said Olivia. “It’s the best thing in the world. I think being Apple’s Artist of the Year feels really amazing. To be recognized as an artist that’s made an impact is really cool.”

“What sets Olivia apart is that she speaks from the heart, every time,” said Rachel Newman, Apple Music’s co-head. “Her songs make you want to call a friend, dance in your kitchen, and tell someone you love them. She is open and genuine in everything she shares, and that connection is what turned a great year into a defining one.”

As Apple Music’s Artist of the Year, Olivia will receive a physical award that represents the extraordinary artistry integral to creating music. Each Apple Music Award features Apple’s custom silicon wafer suspended between a polished sheet of glass, and a machined and anodized aluminum body. In a symbolic gesture, the same chip powering the devices that put over 100 million songs at listeners’ fingertips also sits at the very heart of the Apple Music Awards.

cards.summary: 【Hugging Face 官方动态】Nemotron-Personas-Finance-Japan: A Synthetic Dataset Capturing Japan's Demographics and Financial Context
fulltext: A compound AI approach to Japanese personas grounded in real-world distributions

In the financial sector, the utilization of real-world data faces significant constraints due to strict privacy regulations, compliance requirements, and the need for advanced domain expertise. In this context, the development of agentic AI in the financial domain requires synthetic data capable of avoiding the risks of using real data while reflecting demographics, household structures, and asset statuses to reproduce diverse, realistic financial scenarios.

To address these challenges, Elith and NVIDIA have released Nemotron-Personas-Finance-Japan, a financial domain extension of the open-source persona dataset "Nemotron-Personas-Japan." To our knowledge, it is the first open persona dataset at million-record scale that pairs Japan’s official statistics with household finance and financial literacy data. Built upon official government statistics, this dataset was developed using NeMo SDG-PGMs, a probabilistic graphical model framework for synthetic data generation (SDG), and NeMo Data Designer, an enterprise synthetic data generation system. Furthermore, to enhance the practical utility of the dataset in financial use cases, it was designed by incorporating insights and feedback provided by leading domestic financial institutions and industry associations, including Sompo Japan, Tokio Marine Holdings, Bank of Fukuoka, Mizuho Financial Group, Meiji Yasuda Life Insurance, and the Financial Data Utilization Association (FDUA).

This dataset expands the environment where Japanese developers and enterprises can develop and evaluate AI tailored to local and industry requirements, without using real customer data. Released under the CC BY 4.0 license, it is available for commercial use. From building conversational agents to customer simulation and model evaluation, it supports practical financial AI development. The Nemotron-Personas collection, including Nemotron-Personas-Finance-Japan, is designed to seamlessly integrate with the user simulation framework NeMo User Sim, enabling instant execution of simulations drawn from diverse distributions consistent with the real world.

It was built using NVIDIA’s framework for synthetic data generation, NeMo Data Designer. This compound AI system enables complex Jinja templating, Pydantic validation, structured outputs, automated retries, and support for multiple generation backends. This is the essential toolset required for generating such large-scale synthetic datasets. In addition, the following models were utilized:
Nemotron-Personas-Finance-Japan was designed to align with Japan's official demographic and labor statistics while taking into account key considerations essential for AI training:

Every persona is fully synthetic. No real individuals are represented, and the dataset is designed to reduce privacy risk. Demographics and household finances follow official statistics and public survey data, and names follow real Japanese naming patterns. Personas are built from these distributions, not from records about real people.

Nemotron-Personas-Finance-Japan is built first for teams creating financial AI in Japan, at banks and insurers and at the startups and integrators that serve them. Each persona carries household finances and financial literacy alongside demographics. Teams can use them to build customer-service agents, evaluate sales conversations/marketing initiatives, run user simulations in NeMo User Sim, and red-team customer-facing AI.

The release also serves anyone building for Japanese users. It holds 9M personas, 50% more than Nemotron-Personas-Japan, across 50 fields instead of 22. That gives any Japanese-language project finer slices of the population to train and test on.
The synthetic personas in this dataset can be leveraged for:

Access to diverse, high-quality training data that reflects real-world populations has long been a challenge in AI development. Enterprise AI development has predominantly relied on private data, creating barriers for researchers, startups, and particularly AI developers in regions with limited available data.

By releasing Nemotron-Personas-Finance-Japan under CC BY 4.0, we provide access to enterprise-grade, high-quality synthetic data, empowering anyone to build culturally grounded AI systems with lower cost and less privacy risk.

Nemotron-PII-Japan launches the same day. It holds 100,000 synthetic Japanese business documents with labeled personal information, for training and testing detection and redaction models. Its documents are built on Nemotron-Personas-Japan. Use Nemotron-Personas-Finance-Japan to simulate customers, and Nemotron-PII-Japan to test how your pipeline protects their data.

From teams building AI in Japan to global developers aiming for broader regional deployment, Nemotron-Personas-Finance-Japan dataset provides the authentic, privacy-conscious foundation required for your applications.

fulltext: “过去几个月，各家都在拼命证明AI越来越能干活。但说实话，一个人能干活，不代表一群人就能协作。”
一位长期关注AI办公的业内人士，试用完市面上主流的AI办公产品后发现，有些“麻烦”还是绕不开，最典型的就是有些活儿还得靠人工来回“倒腾”。
“Agent能独立完成任务，但很难接住任务在人与人之间的流转。”有时候，AI交付结果后，人跟人之间交接，比Agent自己干那一步更费时间，也更费心力。
AI办公要打To B的仗，就得正视这一困境。
在AI这件事上，企业真正关心的无非两件：一是个人生产力，AI能不能替员工多干点活；二是组织生产力，AI能不能减少团队协作里的信息损耗和重复劳动。
过去几个月，AI办公在个人生产力上已经跨过不少卡点，但组织生产力这一关，明显还任重而道远。
11月9日，千问办公发布2.0版本，推出行业首个支持多人与Agent协作的功能“协作”，并在官方博客中宣布迈向Team Agent时代，想回应的正是上述的难题：企业的组织生产力，如何跟上个人生产力的提升？
国内AI办公热已经持续了近半年。C端市场的产品竞争日趋激烈，而B端市场的挑战，远不止把产品卖给企业那么简单。
从产品侧看，随着Muse、Cue、Dots等海外Personal Agent产品集中涌现，个人AI的能力边界正在被迅速拓宽，企业级AI也被推到了更高的期待之下。
AI办公厂商正在面临更为严峻的考验：当AI已经能够成为个人的工作搭档，它能否再往前走一步，成为团队协作的一部分？
从客户侧看，企业也有很现实的诉求：买来的AI办公席位，怎么才能真正变成组织生产力？
雷峰网观察到，此前的席位制更像一个准入和预算工具，解决的是“谁能用、用多少”的问题。当AI逐渐成为数字员工，席位制的价值也需要重新定义：从给员工配置AI，转向把员工接入一套人机协作体系。
千问办公2.0一个比较直观的功能，是支持多人和同一个Agent协作。
雷峰网(公众号：雷峰网)用这项功能模拟了一次记者、资深编辑和Agent（千问小Q）一起讨论FDE选题的过程。
在收到“根据已有采访素材，策划FDE相关选题”的指令后，千问小Q自动读取空间资料区的四份采访素材，列出了6个行业观察稿选题和1个备选人物选题，还给出了风险提示。
之后，在记者和资深编辑的讨论中，千问小Q会同时参考两个人的意见，不断完善选题框架。
体验下来，最直观的变化是，参与讨论的人不再需要反复向Agent补充背景。它既能读取空间内的资料，也能跟上多人讨论中的信息变化。原本分散在人与人之间、人与AI之间的信息，现在能够汇集到同一个协作空间里。
但媒体讨论选题是相对轻量化的场景，在银泰百货的调研中，雷峰网看到了多人、多群、多环节的业务协作场景：
银泰百货的团购券业务尤为复杂——62家以上门店、200多名协作人员，每张团购券上架前都要核对约50项资料。这些信息原本散落在60多个钉钉群里，工作人员得反复翻聊天记录、手动汇总进度。
内测使用千问办公2.0的“协作”功能后，团队把这些群聊和卡券AI表格关联到同一个协作空间。千问小Q不仅能汇总进度、更新表格，还能定时检查待办事项，提醒具体负责人。
雷峰网观察到，Team Agent改变的不仅是人和AI的协作关系，还有任务的发起方式和完成方式。
AI办公大多遵循一套相对固定的流程：人提需求，AI执行，人再检查结果。即便Agent已经能自主执行一些任务，工作节奏仍然主要由人驱动。
但这一模式正在发生变化。
此前，Anthropic推出Claude Tag，将Claude引入Slack，让AI以团队成员的身份参与频道里的日常工作。它能够读取所在频道的上下文、调用组织授权的工具，还可以在任务完成时主动同步进展，跟进停滞的讨论和未解决的任务。
这代表了一种产品探索方向：以团队协作频道为入口，让AI成为多人可以共同调用、持续交办任务的工作成员。
千问办公2.0则依托钉钉的企业协作生态，将钉钉群聊、资料空间、AI表格等能力连接起来，让Agent围绕具体业务资料和任务节点参与讨论、汇总进度、跟进待办。
把两者放在一起看，不难发现，AI办公正呈现出一种新趋势：Agent正在从被动响应指令的工具，变成能够主动承接任务、参与工作过程的协作者。
AI如何与“人”共舞，重塑工作流程？在此次千问办公2.0的体验中，雷峰网有两个发现：
一是人机共创：从交付结果，到共同完成工作
过去，人与AI的协作多少有些像接力赛：员工把需求交给AI，等待它生成结果，再将结果复制出来，放进文档或其他工具中继续修改。AI负责生成，人负责判断、调整和整合。
中间多了一道交接，工作也容易被切成两段。
千问办公2.0的同屏编辑，试图让人和AI之间来回传结果这一步消失。
实际体验如何？雷峰网此次让千问办公审校一份FDE初稿：千问办公给出意见后，雷峰网在文档中划出对应的错别字和语病（意见1），再让AI调整部分内容的位置（意见2），以及将文章第一部分划分成两部分（意见3）。
AI批量处理了这三条修改意见，一次性在原文档上直接修改，省去了过去反复复制文字、描述需求、切换软件的工作量。
这和过去让AI生成一份完整文档、再由人接手修改不太一样：人可以随时提出意见，Agent围绕意见持续完善，双方一起把一份作品“磨”出来。
二是自动任务：Agent从等人派活，到主动服务
传统AI办公有一个隐形前提：绝大多数任务，都依赖“人”来主动发起。
这也是当前不少Agent还没跨过去的一道坎。Google Research今年发布的一篇综述论文指出，尽管许多Agent已经具备推理、规划、调用工具和执行复杂任务的能力，但仍然依赖人类识别值得处理的工作、发起任务。
换言之，AI可以接手执行，但还没有真正接过任务发起的主动权。
这也是留给AI办公厂商的探索空间。AI能不能从等待员工派活，走向根据任务条件主动提供服务？
千问办公2.0在功能更新中回应了这个问题。“自动任务”支持触发式任务，用一句自然语言把触发条件和处理要求说清楚，任务就能自动跑起来。
雷峰网也尝试了让千问办公监测钉钉群里更新的采访纪要，主动总结要点并返回群内，省去了以往在AI工具和IM系统中来回“倒腾”的麻烦。
跳出产品视角，从行业角度看，千问办公2.0这次更新也在释放新的信号。
过去几个月，各家厂商不断整合Agent产品、调配组织资源，“集中精力办大事”——靠生态和桌面触点，争夺用户使用AI的入口。
不难看出，上一阶段主要是“横向”收拢战线、先抢入口。但入口之争还没结束，竞争的重心已经开始往“纵向”偏移：谁能让Agent在企业流程里被真正调度起来。
从近期国内AI办公产品的迭代方向看，不少厂商已经意识到，得先把自身能力做深。千问办公从1.0到2.0，恰好落在这一方向上。
“这有点像一个Agent OS。”一位参与内测的企业用户直观感受到：千问办公2.0不只是做了一个更强的AI办公入口，还在尝试让Agent成为连接用户、工具与业务的中间层。
就像传统操作系统调度应用和计算资源，Agent OS调度的是不同工具、数据资源和Agent能力。用户把任务交给千问小Q后，这位“数字员工”会理解需求、调度能力，推动任务往前走。
对企业而言，这意味着数字员工正在成为组织分工中的新参与者。
此前的AI更像是员工手边的助手，帮忙写文档、做分析、整理资料。当Agent能理解业务上下文、调用不同工具，并在多个任务之间持续推进工作时，它就有机会承接一部分原本需要不同岗位接力完成的工作，帮企业减少跨部门沟通和流程衔接中的损耗。
对国内AI办公行业来说，这是一次值得关注的尝试：虽然离真正的Agent OS还有距离，但千问办公已经在拓宽“办公”的边界。
一位从业30余年的To B老兵，曾在今年10月千问办公推出电商版时对雷峰网表示：“当AI办公不再局限于办公的时候，它才真正具有了生命力。”
言下之意，传统的文档、PPT、文案等通用办公能力，很难形成足够强的用户粘性。Agent的价值不只是完成一个通用任务，更在于进入数字世界里的具体业务场景，理解业务数据、规则和工作流程，像真人一样操作不同功能，推动任务真正落地。
这背后，需要AI办公产品进一步打通企业已有的数据与流程。
据了解，IM与Office的融合已在千问办公2.0落地。随着更多钉钉原子能力、SaaS及专业工具逐步接入，千问办公也在尝试减少跨工具操作，让Agent更深入地参与企业真实工作。
这也意味着，Agent OS比拼的不只是接入多少工具，更是能否把工具背后的业务能力组织起来。AI办公产品要从通用任务走向真实业务，还需要专业软件厂商的参与，以及更深层的数据和上下文连接。
说到底，入口决定谁被看见，能不能真正进入企业流程，决定谁被留下。

cards.title: Jonathan Kanter is using AI to take on Big Tech
cards.title_cn: 乔纳森·坎特（ Jonathan Kanter ）正在使用人工智能来对抗大型
cards.summary: 【The Verge】When Jonathan Kanter stepped down as head of the Justice Department's Antitrust Division in 2024, he set out to keep fighting to dismantle illegal monopolies. But this time, he's continuing the fight…
fulltext: The former DOJ watchdog wants to fuel antitrust cases against all kinds of monopolists.

When Jonathan Kanter stepped down as head of the Justice Department’s Antitrust Division in 2024, he set out to keep fighting to dismantle illegal monopolies. But this time, he’s continuing the fight in the private sector, and with a perhaps unexpected tool: AI.

Alongside former acting Antitrust Division chief Doha Mekki, Kanter recently launched a new tech startup, FluxCap. The team is stacked with former DOJ staffers and former Palantir engineers, and it’s selling an AI-based legal research and analysis tool that helps plaintiffs build and strengthen cases against the kinds of well-heeled companies Kanter and Mekki took on at the Antitrust Division. FluxCap is launching with a focus on antitrust cases, but it plans to expand into other practice areas as well.
Kanter imagines FluxCap as a “force multiplier” for antitrust watchdogs taking on powerful opponents in Big Tech and elsewhere.
“This, to me, it’s existential”

“This, to me, it’s existential,” he tells The Verge in an interview. “Because it’s the only way that enforcement is going to work in the long term, is if technology and other tools are able to help scarce resources go significantly further than they can today.”

FluxCap’s platform, built off proprietary technology and existing large language models, is primarily intended for research and analysis. It’s trained to pick up the facts and legal framework that will determine whether a case succeeds, then find potential holes in attorneys’ logic. To help attorneys prepare for trial, FluxCap can also help sift through vast piles of discovery materials, searching for signals that a company acted in anticompetitive ways. It’s part of a wave of legal tech tools that are using AI to try to help lawyers do more with less and make the legal process more efficient.

Getting the tool to find relevant evidence was one of the hardest parts, Kanter says. Executives are unlikely to come out and say they’re monopolists, but surrounding context can give a very specific meaning to certain messages. In the antitrust trial against Live Nation-Ticketmaster, for example, the government played a recorded phone call between the Live Nation CEO and a customer who decided to switch to a different ticketing platform. In response, the CEO reminded the customer that a new arena in town could make it harder to deliver as many concerts to his venue. The customer testified he took it as a “not-so-veiled” threat that Live Nation could cut off events programming if he didn’t also accept its ticketing service.

FluxCap’s team of former government lawyers spent months testing the system with existing and hypothetical test cases to see if it could really help build a solid argument. Getting “basic legal tools” (which Kanter calls “BLTs”) to understand that kind of nuance is difficult because “lawyering isn’t about right or wrong answers,” he says. “Both sides can be right and both sides can be wrong. And what you’re essentially trying to do is you’re trying to persuade a court, a jury, a regulator to reach a certain outcome.”

The team counts antitrust boutique firm Kressin Powers as one of its first customers, and Kanter says it’s in talks with both public and private enforcers. “It gives them that virtual capacity so that a small team can take on a large team,” Kanter says, adding that it provides the manpower of roughly “20-plus people working around the clock.”

The seeds of FluxCap began inside the Antitrust Division, where Kanter and his team were already trying to stretch their limited resources with technology. During the Biden administration, the DOJ went to trial against Google twice and brought monopolization suits against Apple and Live Nation, among other actions. But the Division’s resources and staff pale in comparison to companies with multibillion- to trillion-dollar market caps and large legal teams to review documents and mount defenses. The entire Antitrust Division was appropriated $245 million by Congress for fiscal year 2026, with more than 400 attorneys on staff across several issue areas.
“It’s just not realistic to have the resources necessary to take on these big companies”

The imbalance is even greater for state attorneys general, who have pushed forward with antitrust action as the Trump administration has hung back. Earlier this year, state AGs won a case against Live Nation that the DOJ under the Trump administration settled, and states also sued to block the Paramount-Warner Media merger before ultimately settling, when the DOJ declined. “A large state AG might have 10 people working on a case,” Kanter says. “It’s just not realistic to have the resources necessary to take on these big companies.”

During Kanter’s time as antitrust head, he and others tried AI-based BLTs but found them lacking for complex legal research. “Every antitrust lawyer has tried asking questions to ChatGPT or [AI legal research software] Harvey or one of those tools, and they do okay,” Kanter says. “But they miss the nuance.” While Kanter was at the DOJ, the Antitrust Division secured a $45.5 million grant from the government’s Tech Modernization Fund to implement better tools for managing cases and reviewing evidence. Kanter says his team “never had the opportunity to put that to work” before leaving office, but what they’re building now is “even more ambitious and better than I could have imagined when I was at DOJ.”

Tech alone can’t fully even the playing field, Kanter says. “Government is always going to be outmatched, and they desperately need more funding, and desperately need more budget, and more headcount.” Even if that happens, however, private defendants are likely to “far outweigh anything that the government could ever produce, whether it’s federal government or states or private plaintiffs,” he says. “We believe this will be the great equalizer that will allow those teams to go toe to toe with anyone regardless of their size and regardless how deep their pockets are.”

fulltext_cn: 这家前司法部监管机构希望推动针对各种垄断者的反垄断案件。
当乔纳森·坎特（ Jonathan Kanter ）于2024年辞去司法部反垄断部门负责人职务时，他着手继续努力消除非法垄断。但这一次，他继续在私营部门进行斗争，并使用了一个可能出乎意料的工具：人工智能。
坎特与前代理反垄断部门负责人多哈·梅基（ Doha Mekki ）一起，最近推出了一家新的科技创业公司FluxCap。该团队由前司法部工作人员和前Palantir工程师组成，他们正在销售基于人工智能的法律研究和分析工具，帮助原告建立和加强针对Kanter和Mekki在反垄断部门所涉富裕公司的案件。FluxCap正在以反垄断案件为重点推出，但它计划扩展到其他实践领域。
坎特将FluxCap想象为反垄断监管机构在大型科技公司和其他地方对抗强大对手的“力量倍增器”。
“对我来说，这是存在主义”
“对我来说，这是存在主义，”他在接受采访时告诉The Verge。“因为从长远来看，这是执法工作的唯一途径，如果技术和其他工具能够帮助稀缺的资源比现在更进一步。”
FluxCap的平台建立在专有技术和现有大型语言模型的基础上，主要用于研究和分析。它经过培训，能够掌握确定案件是否成功的事实和法律框架，然后在律师的逻辑中发现潜在的漏洞。为了帮助律师为审判做好准备， FluxCap还可以帮助筛选大量的发现材料，寻找公司以反竞争方式行事的信号。这是一波法律技术工具的一部分，这些工具正在使用人工智能来帮助律师以更少的资源做更多的事情，并提高法律程序的效率。

Kanter说，获得找到相关证据的工具是最困难的部分之一。高管们不太可能站出来说自己是垄断者，但周围环境可以为某些信息赋予非常具体的含义。例如，在对Live Nation-Ticketmaster的反垄断审判中，政府播放了Live Nation首席执行官和决定切换到不同票务平台的客户之间的录音电话。作为回应，首席执行官提醒客户，在城里新建一个舞台可能会使向他的场地提供尽可能多的音乐会变得更加困难。该客户作证说，他认为这是一个“不那么隐蔽”的威胁，如果他不接受其票务服务， Live Nation可能会切断活动节目。
FluxCap的前政府律师团队花了数月时间用现有和假设的测试案例测试该系统，看看它是否真的有助于建立一个坚实的论据。他说，让“基本法律工具” （坎特称之为“BLT” ）理解这种细微差别很困难，因为“律师工作不是关于正确或错误的答案”。“双方都可能是正确的，双方都可能是错误的。你本质上要做的是试图说服法院、陪审团和监管机构达成某种结果。”
该团队将反垄断精品公司Kressin Powers视为其首批客户之一， Kanter表示正在与公共和私人执法机构进行谈判。Kanter说： “这给了他们这种虚拟能力，这样一个小团队就可以承担一个大团队的工作。”他补充说，这提供了大约“20多名全天候工作的人力。”
FluxCap的种子始于反垄断部门， Kanter和他的团队已经在试图用技术来扩展他们有限的资源。在拜登政府期间，司法部两次对谷歌提起诉讼，并对苹果和Live Nation提起垄断诉讼。但与拥有数十亿至万亿美元市值的公司和大型法律团队来审查文件并进行辩护的公司相比，该部门的资源和员工相形见绌。国会为整个反垄断部门拨款2.45亿美元($) ，用于2026财年，在多个问题领域有400多名律师。
“拥有必要的资源来对抗这些大公司是不现实的”
对于州检察长来说，这种不平衡甚至更大，随着特朗普政府的退缩，他们已经推进了反垄断行动。今年早些时候，各州政府赢得了针对Live Nation的案件，特朗普政府下的司法部达成和解，各州还起诉阻止派拉蒙-华纳媒体合并，然后在司法部拒绝时最终解决。Kanter说：「一家大型州立股份公司可能有10人处理一个案件。“拥有必要的资源来对抗这些大公司是不现实的。”

在坎特担任反垄断负责人期间，他和其他人尝试了基于人工智能的BLT ，但发现它们缺乏复杂的法律研究。Kanter说： “每个反垄断律师都曾尝试向ChatGPT或[AI法律研究软件] Harvey或其中一个工具提问，他们做得很好。”“但他们错过了细微差别。“当坎特在司法部工作时，反垄断部门从政府的技术现代化基金获得了4550万美元的赠款，用于实施更好的案件管理和证据审查工具。坎特说，在离开办公室之前，他的团队“从来没有机会把它付诸实践” ，但他们现在正在建设的是“比我在司法部时所能想象的更雄心勃勃、更好”。
Kanter说，仅靠技术还不能充分发挥作用。“政府总是比不上，他们迫切需要更多的资金，迫切需要更多的预算和更多的员工。“然而，即使发生这种情况，私人被告也可能“远远超过政府可以生产的任何东西，无论是联邦政府还是各州或私人原告，”他说。“我们相信这将是一个伟大的均衡器，使这些团队能够与任何人齐头并进，无论他们的规模有多大，无论他们的口袋有多深。”
